metric.diagnostics.machine_readable_interface: 'quidra check program.qui --json' emits {ok, truncated, diagnostics:[{code, message, file, span:{start,end line/column}}]}; --max-errors N controls the emission limit (default 20) and JSON reports truncation.
metric.diagnostics.method: Direct inspection of docs/spec/diagnostics.md (stable code catalogue) plus live compiler runs of quidra 0.3.0 via 'quidra check FILE --json' and 'quidra run FILE' on constructed failing programs.
metric.diagnostics.normalization: 0-100 scale, 100 = best-in-class diagnostics among evaluated languages (e.g. Rust-level). 88 reflects a mature, coded, spanned, machine-readable diagnostic system with unified compile/runtime failure taxonomy, scored slightly below top-tier established compilers only for unconfirmed absence of secondary/related-span notes and inline fix-it suggestions in the sampled JSON.
strengths: stable, versioned diagnostic codes decoupled from wording (contract explicitly documented: 'message wording may become more specific without changing the code')
every diagnostic carries a source span (line/column start/end)
machine-readable JSON diagnostics interface built into the compiler CLI, not a third-party add-on
deterministic, coded runtime safety failures (status 101) with the same code+span discipline extended into runtime, unifying compile-time and runtime diagnosability
conservative error recovery (invalid type propagation) documented to avoid cascading spurious diagnostics from one root cause
explicit control over diagnostic volume via --max-errors with truncation reporting in JSON

metric.functionality_expressiveness.comparative_note: Union types, exhaustiveness checking, per-field flow-sensitive initialization tracking across interprocedural summaries, and a restricted ABI-safe FFI surface are language-level design choices comparable in ambition to Rust/Kotlin sum types and Rust's FFI safety subset; scored below top established languages only where advanced generic metaprogramming (e.g. higher-kinded types, trait objects, reflection) is absent from the current spec.
features_confirmed_present: generic classes with constrained type parameters (numeric/integer/floating/ordered/equatable constraints)
first-class tagged unions (T | U) with flattening/canonicalization and none/error alternatives
exhaustive structural match over union alternatives (MATCH_EXHAUSTIVE enforced)
arbitrary precision numeric types (bigint, bigreal) alongside fixed-width int8..uint64/float32/float64
tensor and neural built-in types with shape patterns and static shape checking (TENSOR_SHAPE)
error as a first-class typed value plus try-propagation (TRY_CONTEXT) instead of exceptions
definite-initialization / uninitialized-field flow analysis integrated into the type system (per-field summaries across constructors/returns)
const/writable reference contracts with path-local const and explicit authority rules (WRITE_CAPABILITY)
FFI/extern declarations with a restricted, explicit ABI-safe subset (FFI_TYPE, FFI_CALLBACK_TYPE, FFI_REFERENCE codes)
CLI declaration block sugar (cli decl with argument/option/flag sources)
structured bin (packed bit) type distinct from byte arrays, with explicit bit-level operations
default parameters, named arguments, arity/order rules enforced by ARGUMENT_MISMATCH/DUPLICATE_ARGUMENT
module/import system with cycle detection (IMPORT_CYCLE) and package version/ABI compatibility checks (PACKAGE_COMPATIBILITY)
REPL with session-safety guard against replaying nondeterministic effects (REPL_REPLAY_UNSAFE)
limitations_observed: no operator overloading or user-defined implicit conversions found in the spec
no trait objects / dynamic dispatch across unrelated types beyond union match
generic constraints are a fixed closed set (numeric/integer/floating/ordered/equatable), not user-extensible interfaces

metric.functionality_expressiveness.method: Feature survey against docs/spec/language.md and docs/spec/grammar.ebnf, cross-checked against the built quidra 0.3.0 compiler ('quidra check --json') for accepted/rejected syntax.
metric.functionality_expressiveness.normalization: 0-100 scale, 100 = maximally expressive among evaluated languages; 78 reflects strong modern feature set (unions, exhaustive match, generics, tensors/neural built-ins, structured FFI) offset by absence of user-defined traits/interfaces and operator overloading.
